extracted.subtask_description: Reporting of military operations and related events during wartime for a general newspaper audience, including references to operational security, official communiqués, correspondent restrictions, and transmission methods. Emphasizes how and why certain details are withheld or censored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational security / radio silence
rubrics_metrics.description: Radio silence must be observed by ships of the attacking forces; certain results of attacks 'have not been disclosed because radio silence must be observed by ships of the attacking forces.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not publish or disclose tactical or timing details of ongoing naval/air operations when commanders require radio silence. Reports should note that details are being withheld for security (example: 'the result of which has not been disclosed because radio silence must be observed').

rubrics_metrics.name: Censorship of correspondents and restrictions on filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondents were not permitted to use the radio for three days and were at times 'not permitted to write stories at the time concerning the beachhead operations' because their dispatches had allegedly caused alarm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commands may temporarily restrict reporters' communication (radio, filing) during sensitive operations. Editors and correspondents must comply with such embargoes or use approved channels; expect temporary prohibitions on filing and the possibility of later lifted restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain perspective; avoid unduly pessimistic or distorted dispatches
rubrics_metrics.description: The Army cut off radio use because dispatches 'showed complete lack of perspective and distorted the facts' and were 'unduly pessimistic'—causing 'unjustified alarm among the people.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists should frame battlefield reports with appropriate context and avoid language that could create undue public alarm; maintain accuracy and balance to prevent censorship or loss of transmission privileges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rely on and signal limits of official communiqués / preliminary reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Official communiqués often give succinct, provisional information (e.g., 'Our forces have captured...' and 'Preliminary reports indicate our casualties have been light'). They may omit fuller details such as enemy fleet size or full results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using military communiqués, report their provisional nature and the possibility of omitted details. Attribute claims to the communiqué and avoid inferring specifics that the release does not provide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use alternative transmission methods when communications are restricted
rubrics_metrics.description: When radio use was denied, dispatches 'were sent out of the beachhead by courier' and correspondents filed by courier rather than radio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to use couriers or other non-electronic means when electronic communications are restricted; note the method of transmission in reporting when relevant to explain delays or limited detail.
